decisions: A variable introduced by a standalone typed instance selector `Kind//$x;` remains available to following statements for the rest of the same CFEL block. A variable newly introduced in an IF condition is scoped to that condition and its matching THEN group only. Mixed AND/OR requires explicit parentheses, with no implicit precedence. A new IF binding must use a different name from any already bound outer variable; references to an outer binding retain its identity.

new_previews.changes: Group one CFEL expression; parentheses do not create a Node or Relation. When AND and OR occur in one Boolean expression, use parentheses to make their grouping explicit; neither has implicit precedence over the other.
new_previews.limits: No claim about outer variable lifetime, shadowing or new syntax.

new_previews.changes: Standalone typed instance selector `Kind//$x;` binding lasts through following statements in the same CFEL block; an IF-introduced binding is local to its condition and matching THEN group; a new binding must use a different name from an already bound outer variable, and references preserve existing identity.
new_previews.limits: No claim about outer variable lifetime, shadowing or new syntax.

resolved_standalone_binding.question: How long does a variable introduced by a standalone selector remain bound: through the rest of its CFEL fenced block, or only in the statement where it is introduced?
resolved_standalone_binding.example: R2462 instance block has `Node//$node;` followed by `($node, $node.**) {:0}((*));` and further statements using $node. The settled IF rule applies only to variables introduced in IF and does not resolve this standalone use.
resolved_standalone_binding.blast_radius: Current declaration patterns that bind standalone instances and reuse names in later expressions, including R2462 and R2701; determines validity and evaluation without affecting the settled IF rule.
resolved_standalone_binding.resolution: A variable introduced by a standalone typed instance selector `Kind//$x;` is available to following statements for the rest of the same CFEL block; specified once in R2604, not restated in R2462 or R2701.

next_question.question: What syntax distinguishes literal text from names and operators inside CFEL, especially for multiword values and special characters?
next_question.example: R2601 uses the quoted token "()" while R2707 uses unquoted multiword value Scope Contract; R1931 specifies backslash escaping and says quotes are carrier serialization for Entity names. Those facts do not fully define CFEL literal boundaries.
next_question.blast_radius: Literal values, escaped operator characters, multiword enum values and parsing of formatted claims. Subject-path escaping alone does not define all CFEL literal contexts.
